transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-05
Start time: 10:00 PT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kaplan (CEO), Aisha Patel (Head of Product), Liam O'Connor (VP Eng), Maya Singh (CRO), Sofia Ramos (Head of People), Nina Park (Security), plus ~150 Redwood employees

Summary:
Leadership update on Q2 performance, Q3 priorities, product roadmap highlights (Dedicated, Private, Optimize), hiring and org changes, security/SOC2 status, and open Q&A. Quick wins and metrics shared.

Topics:
- Business performance & ARR cadence
- Product: roadmap, Dedicated capacity and Private deployment updates, Optimize features
- Reliability & latency work (P99 focus)
- Security & compliance (SOC2 status, KMS/HSM integrations)
- Hiring and people ops updates
- Q&A and next steps

Action items (captured verbally): see metadata action_items

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Good morning, good afternoon depending where you are. We got about an hour, we'll go through a quick leadership update and then open the floor for Q&A.
[00:15] Jordan: Quick logistical note - recording is on, and we'll post the deck and the video to the all-hands channel after.
[00:30] Aisha: Hi team. I'm gonna start with product. Last quarter we shipped the initial autoscaling policies for Dedicated, and the early feedback from customers has been great on predictable throughput. There's a couple of follow ups: we need better visibility in the Console for burst usage and per-route breakdowns.
[00:48] Aisha: On Private，we finished the VPC control plane prototype with one pilot customer, the on-prem installer still has a couple of wrinkles—namely network interface mapping on older firewalls. We're tracking that in the ticket 4492.
[01:10] Liam: On the runtime side, we've made progress on kernel selection heuristics and quantization profiles. The continuous batching improvements reduced cost-per-token for long-running sessions by about 12% in our internal bench. Note: some of the numbers are rough, bench environments vary.
[01:30] Speaker 1: Can you explain the tradeoffs between Dedicated and Hosted for latency-sensitive customers?
[01:36] Maya: Great question. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and isolation, so for strict latency SLOs you can tune instance sizes. Hosted is simpler and often lower time-to-value but shared capacity can cause jitter under extreme bursts. There are also routing policies we use to fallback to cheaper variants during high load.
[01:55] Jordan: On go-to-market, we saw a nice bump in self-serve conversion after the new quickstart templates. Maya will share more in the GTM section.
[02:05] Maya: Quick numbers: sign-ups up 18% month-over-month, self-serve conversion up 2 points. Enterprise pipeline: we've got three POCs moving to pilot with target start dates in late August. The big ask here is more reference architecture docs for security teams — customers keep asking for SSO/SAML and audit log examples.
[02:28] Nina: On compliance - SOC2: we closed a number of control gaps and the auditor is coming back for a readiness check mid-August. KMS/HSM integrations are in the roadmap; we've done initial testing with two vendors but need to standardize the key rotation docs. Also note we had a note about unclear transcript in the last audit call — "K V cache" often came through in notes as "K V cache" and it confused the reviewers.
[02:57] Liam: Reliability update - P99 latency focus: we've been running synthetic and customer-real workloads through the new batcher. There's one regression we saw with short sequence workloads that increases tail latency; we have a patch queued and a canary rolling out today.
[03:20] Aisha: Product priorities for Q3
- Launch: improved Console route-level cost breakdown and burst insights
- Launch: Private GA for small on-prem customers (limited) with better installer docs
- Experiment: Optimize recommendations for quantization and batching profiles exposed in Console
[03:40] Jordan: Financials, briefly. ARR growth healthy, revenue a little under plan this quarter due to enterprise contract timing. We still closed a couple of notable logos and expansion ARR was decent. Cash runway extended with the recent Series C tranche, so we can keep investing in product and reliability.
[04:05] Sofia: People update: hiring remains a top priority. We're focused on mid-senior ICs for runtime and infra. We also launched a new referral bonus program, and our DEI training calendar is set for September. Please fill out the hiring interest form so we can prioritize internal mobility.
[04:25] Jordan: Quick note on core differentiators - we keep hearing customers value the combination of runtime performance and the unified dev experience. Competitive landscape: OpenAI and Anthropic are cited often; enterprise buyers ask about on-prem and VPC which is where our Private story matters.
[04:48] Audience: (chatter) applause, thumbs up emoji in chat
[05:00] Q&A:
[05:02] Speaker 2: Hi, question about cost controls - will we have recommended quantization settings per model in the Console?
[05:10] Aisha: Yes, that's the Optimize effort - recommend quantization and batching profiles based on your workload. We're starting with three model archetypes and plan to expand. It's going to be both auto-suggested and manual override.
[05:26] Speaker 3: Regarding Private: what's the expected timeline for GA?
[05:30] Aisha: We're aiming for a limited GA in Q3, broader availability in Q4. Shipping will be gated on installer stability, audit docs, and a small set of pilot customers.
[05:45] Speaker 4: Security question - are we supporting BYOK (bring your own key) for Private?
[05:50] Nina: Short answer: yes for Private via KMS/HSM integration. For Hosted we plan customer-managed keys via KMS but some of the controls are EOD. We're targeting full BYOK documentation by mid-August.
[06:05] Speaker 5: Any changes to support SLAs for Dedicated customers?
[06:10] Maya: We're formalizing SLA tiers for Dedicated — latency and uptime SLOs tied to reserved capacity levels. Those will be part of the Dedicated contracts and we hope to publish initial SLA bands in the next two weeks.
[06:28] Jordan: Ok, we're going to switch to a short demo of the new Console route insights. Aisha, take it away.
[06:33] Aisha: I'll share my screen. (screen share noise) So here you can see the per-route cost breakdown, token-level cost, latency histogram, and the burst window. Note: demo uses synthetic traffic.
[07:05] Aisha: There's a new toggle to enable automatic prefix caching for routes that are long-lived. That's the same prefix/K V cache feature we've been iterating on — sometimes notes render as "K V cache" in transcripts.
[07:20] Liam: On the deployment side we've reduced warm-start overhead by ~20% using smarter KV cache warming heuristics. Patch will go to canary tonight.
[07:36] Audience: (applause)
[07:40] Q&A continued:
[07:42] Speaker 6: For Dedicated oversubscription, are we providing any guarantees for burst pricing?
[07:50] Maya: There's a burst policy where you get X capacity at Y price as an optional add-on. Full pricing details will be in the published doc. We'll share examples and math.
[08:05] Speaker 7: A question from sales: what's the best way to position Private to regulated customers?
[08:12] Jordan: Emphasize control and auditability — Private lets you keep data flows inside your network, integrate with KMS, and preserve audit logs. Provide the SOC2 readiness and installer guide to the security reviewer. Also offer a pilot with clear success criteria.
[08:35] Maya: We're also putting together a one-page compliance checklist for sales to share with customers — that'll have the typical questions: SSO, audit logs, encryption at rest and transit, data residency.
[08:50] Jordan: Okay final section, org changes. We are creating a small "Optimize" team that sits between product and research focused on cost/perf tooling — Aisha will lead product and Ethan will be the engineering lead. This team will centralize quantization recommendations, auto-batching heuristics, and the recommendation engine.
[09:18] Aisha: Super excited. We'll be recruiting internally over the next two weeks.
[09:25] Sofia: HR note: we'll run info sessions, and there's a sign-up in the internal jobs board.
[09:33] Open mic:
[09:35] Speaker 8: Congrats to the infra team on the kernel work, saw big improvements in our benchmarks.
[09:40] Liam: Thanks - shout out to the bench team.
[09:45] Speaker 9: Are we tracking token-level costs by customer in the Console?
[09:48] Aisha: Yes, token-level cost is available per-route and we plan to roll out per-customer breakdowns next quarter.
[10:00] Jordan: Alright, two quick administrative things - please fill the all-hands feedback survey, and check the calendar for the town hall in September.
[10:10] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll post notes, the deck and action items.
[10:15] (meeting ends, recording stops)

Notes and artifacts referenced: deck (link: internal://all-hands/2026-08-05-deck), ticket 4492 (internal tracker), Q3 roadmap draft (internal doc link to be published).

End of transcript.
